paragraph: Bogota is a single-family town, plain and simple. Twenty-three houses sold over six months at a median of $640,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.0136 and 57 percent of homes going above asking. Median days on market was 21. That is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving, and buyers should expect company on the good ones without assuming every listing turns into a bidding war. Sales ran from $320,000 to $750,000, so the median is the better guide than the range. Monthly closings stayed in the low single digits, which is too thin to read a real trend. If Bogota follows the usual Bergen County seasonal arc, expect volume to ease through fall. There is essentially no condo or co-op activity here, so the decision isn't which tier. It's which street and how much house you need.
